correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the lower bound including both parities. With excess e and Q=e+1, every length-Q integer window starting at a=0,…,N must hold two one-occurrences, counted with multiplicity, and the outer markers must span at least N zeros. For odd m=2k+1, disjoint windows force N<kQ. For even m=2k they again force N<kQ; when N≥(k−1)Q, the partitions starting at 0 and at r=N−(k−1)Q each exhaust the markers in ordered pairs, hence the first lies at or beyond r and the last at or before kQ−1. Thus 2N<(m−1)Q in every case. In the construction at h=N/(m−1)>0, the floor levels floor(ih) embed a target using the specified ceiling indices: if a=0 then i=1 and the middle gap bound is direct; if a>0 then ih<a+h and jh≥a+b+h. The available suffix is at least c by (m+1−j)h≥c, also when a+b=0 and j=2. Flooring preserves all required integer gaps. The total telescopes to N+floor(2h). For unrestricted length, the product maximum floor(T²/4)≤2N<floor((T+1)²/4) at T=floor(sqrt(8N+1)) proves the exact minimum of k+floor(2N/k); N=0 gives length two separately as well.
residual_risks: The argument concerns scattered subsequences of the complete two-one layer, not contiguous factors, higher weights or arbitrary selected target families.
